newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade murder rate rising sharply in 1997 -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade murder rate rising sharply in 1997 -- paper.

text.p: The number of murders in Yugoslavia's capital Belgrade has risen dramatically this year, jumping to 40 in the first four months of the year from 55 in the whole of 1996, the Belgrade newspapar Politika reported on Monday.
Most of this year's murders were committed with an unregistered firearm and half of them remain unsolved, the pro-government newspaper said, quoting unofficial information.
Statistically, people are most frequently killed on a Tuesday, while only one murder was committed on a Friday - that of Deputy Interior Minister Radovan Stojicic "Badza".
The 46-year-old police general and deputy interior minister was shot by a masked man as he dined with his son in a city restaurant. His killer has not been caught.
Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic has repeatedly vowed a crackdown on crime but there have been no results so far.
Many victims of the city's crime wave were gang leaders, but just as many were ordinary citizens, killed for their money or possessions as Yugoslavia's standard of living continues to decline.
